# Susan Baker

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005)</sub>
- **Status:** unmarried  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005)</sub>
- **Origin:** the Glen  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052)</sub>
- **Role:** maid-of-all-work  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052)</sub>

## Appearance

Susan considers herself plain-looking, though as good-looking as most married women.

_Sources: [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005)_

## Personality

Susan is a grim-faced, pragmatic, and kind-hearted woman. She is fiercely protective of and devoted to the doctor's household, taking charge of chores and comforting Anne when needed. She is somewhat superstitious and holds a soft spot for men, admitting she would have married if given the chance. She also enjoys receiving compliments on her cooking.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005), [v4 c24 P7](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0007), [v4 c24 P9](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0009), [v4 c40 P10](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0010), [v4 c40 P49](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0049)_

## History

Susan Baker, an elderly spinster from the Glen, was installed as maid-of-all-work for Dr. Gilbert Blythe and Anne Shirley at their small house. She took complete charge of running the household, cooking, and looking after Anne's well-being. She formed a quick liking for Owen Ford after he praised her strawberry shortcake. When her sister Matilda broke her leg, Susan temporarily left her duties to go and nurse her. She also vigilantly guarded the house and baby against perceived dangers like stray cats and advised Anne on matters of marriage and practical living.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c19 P41](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0041), [v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003), [v4 c24 P7](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0007), [v4 c31 P15](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0015), [v4 c36 P19](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0019), [v4 c36 P21](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0021), [v4 c40 P10](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0010), [v4 c40 P49](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0049)_

## Quotes

> Susan is at the helm. There is no use in keeping a dog and doing your own barking.  <sub>[v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003)</sub>

> I am an old maid, but you never hear ME abusing the men. I like ’em. I would have married one if I could.  <sub>[v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005)</sub>

> He is as nice as his ears, Mrs. Doctor, dear  <sub>[v4 c24 P7](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0007)</sub>

> And superstition or not, if I find that yellow beast lurking near our baby I will whack him with the poker, Mrs. Doctor, dear.  <sub>[v4 c40 P10](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0010)</sub>

> Well, I never was much hand for weeping, Mrs. Doctor, dear. I would rather fall to and cheer people up than weep with them.  <sub>[v4 c40 P49](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0049)</sub>
